title: 牛油溪 BTA 筛选标准
instruction:
你是中士。埃斯特尔·扎勒夫斯基 (Estelle Zalewski) 与 Tallow Creek 社区学院警察。在第二校区于一月份开放之前，院长 Eamon Merriweather 需要一个可用的行为威胁评估、管理筛选和转介标准。 Bellhaven Partners在`Tallow_Creek_BTAM_source.xlsx`组装了工作材料；它结合了与州学校安全中心、卡文迪什局、县危机小组和大学行为守则相关的摘录和条款草案，但从未被整理成操作文件。使用完全相同的文件名在您开始的工作目录的顶层创建 `Tallow_Creek_BTAM_standard.xlsx`。
该工作手册适用于两个校区的 BTAM 团队，Frida Crowther 和 Dmitri Kaczmarek 在收到疑虑时必须可供使用，Nils Ferreira 在临床反应可能适当时可供使用，以及校园警察在事件可能需要警方采取行动时可供使用。根据提供的材料建立一份简明的筛选和转介标准。在工作簿中对操作要求进行编号，以便审阅者可以遵循它们。包括目的和范围、负责初始筛选和升级的人员或角色、要捕获的信息、明确定义的层级结构、每层的触发或决策基础、每层启动的行动和推荐、文档和后续期望，以及解释该标准如何在两个校区应用的简短部分。
四种源语音不使用相同的阈值或词汇。保留重要的来源事实并确定其来源，但将重叠的条款协调成一个连贯的标准，而不是将四个单独的政策粘贴在一起。如果材料对于何时关注的是警察问题而不是临床转诊至尼尔斯·费雷拉 (Nils Ferreira) 存在分歧，请明确说明管辖选择，并根据所提供的材料给出简短的理由。不要提出诊断、承诺保密或制定消息来源不支持的新法律义务。如果无法自信地协调来源条款，请显示不确定性并确定谁必须做出决定，而不是默默地选择不受支持的事实。
使完成的工作簿易于审核：包括将实质性要求与其原始材料联系起来的来源或人行横道区域、供主管使用的简短实施说明以及供筛选时使用的紧凑决策辅助工具。保持散文的可操作性并避免学术背景。不要将源工作簿中不相关的材料复制到标准中，在解释草案时不要依赖任何退休或辅助字段，并且不要重复重复的规定，就好像它是两个单独的要求一样。保持源工作簿不变；请勿添加虚构的人员、校园、机构、联系方式、阈值、表格或代码。仅使用摘要或源文件中提供的名称和组织。结果应该足够完整以供监督审查，同时对于一线主管在 1 月之前运行仍保持实用性。

---

上面提到的文件在`references/`中：

- `references/Tallow_Creek_BTAM_source.xlsx` — 提供的单一源工作簿，包含部分完成的 BTAM 草案以及必须忠实提取、归因、协调并转换为所要求的标准的源条款。

将您完成的工作写入**当前工作目录的顶层**，使用以下文件名：
- `Tallow_Creek_BTAM_standard.xlsx` — 一个电子表格，包含已完成的两校区 BTAM 筛选和转介标准、其操作决策辅助、来源人行横道和实施说明。 （完全使用指定的文件名将文件写入起始工作目录的顶层。；保持提供的源工作簿不变。；仅使用提供的工作簿支持的事实以及摘要中的名称和组织。；该标准必须以电子表格形式可读，并且适合监督审查。；不要复制不相关的相邻表或使用已退休的辅助字段作为权威。）

除了这些文件名之外，不会收集任何内容。在其他地方或以任何其他名称编写的正确文件得分为零。

sheets.name: Working material
rows: Bellhaven Partners | Tallow Creek BTAM working material
Use a behavioral threat assessment and management process to identify, assess, manage, and refer concerning behavior. The process is prevention-focused and applies to school settings.
Capture the report source, observed behavior or communication, people or setting affected, timing, and available supporting information. Record facts and distinguish them from speculation.

Initial screening separates information that indicates immediate safety concern, information needing further assessment, and information that can be managed with support and monitoring. Do not use the screen to diagnose.
A concern may be reassessed when new information is received. Threat assessment and management are continuing processes, not a one-time label.
Use a multidisciplinary threat assessment and management review to coordinate assessment, management, and referral when the initial screen indicates a concern needs further review.
Record what was reported, who provided it, when it occurred or was received, the person or location involved, and available messages, images, or other supporting material.

When reported behavior or information indicates an immediate or ongoing safety threat, seek a campus police response and escalate for urgent review. Preserve the reported information and document the action taken.
A law-enforcement response is appropriate for an immediate or ongoing safety threat or information requiring police action; it is not the default response to every concerning behavior.
Document the concern, screening decision, rationale, action, and referral or review path.
Document the concern, screening decision, rationale, action, and referral or review path.
For a clinical referral, provide observed concerns, relevant timing, current setting or location when known, available supporting information, and the reason a clinical response may be appropriate.

Crisis-team intake may be appropriate when reported behavior suggests distress or a need for clinical assessment and the available information does not indicate an immediate or ongoing safety threat requiring police action.
If intake information is incomplete, obtain available clarifying information and identify the responsible reviewer before relying on a clinical referral decision.
Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
A behavioral threat assessment is not a disciplinary finding. Conduct-code review, if warranted by reported behavior, is separate from the assessment and management process.
Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
Reported conduct may be referred for conduct-code review based on the information available. A conduct-code implication does not by itself require a police response.
Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
The conduct code applies to College activities and premises. Apply the same behavioral assessment and management approach wherever the concern is received.
Draft notes: reconcile source language before use.

sheets.name: Standard
rows: Behavioral Threat Assessment and Management (BTAM) Screening and Referral Standard | two-campus use | Owner: Sgt. Estelle Zalewski | Sponsor: Dean Eamon Merriweather
Use this standard to receive, screen, assess, manage, and refer concerning behavior in a prevention-focused process. It is not a general student-conduct policy.
State School-Safety Center; Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code

This standard applies across both campuses whenever a concern is received. Behavioral threat assessment is not a disciplinary finding; a conduct-code review may proceed separately when warranted by reported behavior.
Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
Use observable behavior, communications, and available information. Record what is known and what remains unverified; do not diagnose or treat speculation as fact.
When either receives a concern, initiate the initial screen using the compact decision aid and document the observed information, tier, basis, and disposition.
Review and coordinate assessment, management, referral, and reassessment when the screen indicates further review or the available information does not support a confident tier decision.
State School-Safety Center; County Crisis Team
Provide the police response and urgent escalation path when the screen identifies an immediate or ongoing safety threat or information requiring police action.
Receive a clinical referral when observed information suggests distress or a need for clinical assessment and does not indicate an immediate or ongoing safety threat requiring police action.
Capture what was reported or observed, who provided it, the person or setting affected, timing (occurred or received), and available messages, images, or other supporting material.
Identify observed behavior or communication separately from inferences, missing facts, or speculation. A screen is not a diagnosis.
Assign the tier using the observable decision basis below, then document the screening decision, rationale, action, and referral, review, or monitoring path.
Information does not indicate an immediate or ongoing safety threat and can be managed with support and monitoring on the information available.
Document the disposition and any support or monitoring action; do not automatically refer to campus police.
Retain for monitoring and reassess if new information is received. Conduct-code review may be considered separately when warranted.
State School-Safety Center; Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
Information needs further assessment, or observed information suggests distress or a need for clinical assessment, but does not indicate an immediate or ongoing safety threat requiring police action.
Document the facts, information gap, and preliminary rationale. Obtain available clarifying information.
Refer the clinical intake information to Nils Ferreira; BTAM team coordinates review and reassesses as information is received.
State School-Safety Center; County Crisis Team
Reported behavior or information indicates an immediate or ongoing safety threat, or information requires police action.
Seek campus police response, preserve reported information, and document action taken; escalate for urgent BTAM review.
Campus police response and urgent BTAM review. Reassess management and referral needs as information is received.

Cavendish Bureau governs the police threshold: an immediate or ongoing safety threat, or information requiring police action, starts the campus-police path. County Crisis Team governs clinical intake only when observed information suggests a clinical need and does not indicate that police threshold.
This follows Cavendish Bureau’s direct police boundary while preserving County Crisis Team’s clinical-intake condition. Conduct-code implications alone do not require police action.
Cavendish Bureau; County Crisis Team; Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code

Do not force a tier. Record the missing information, obtain available clarification, and identify the BTAM team for review before relying on a clinical referral decision. Escalate to Tier 3 when the information indicates the urgent trigger.
County Crisis Team; Cavendish Bureau; State School-Safety Center

Document the concern; report source; observed information; affected person or setting; timing; available supporting material; tier; rationale; immediate action; and referral, review, or monitoring path.
BTAM team tracks Tier 2 and Tier 3 management and reassesses when new information is received. Tier 1 dispositions are revisited when new information changes the screening basis.

Supervisors at both campuses use the same intake fields, tier definitions, and decision aid; check that the documented rationale matches the tier and route. Escalation is based on observed information, not campus location.
Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code; State School-Safety Center

Record Tier 3, observed basis, and urgent action. Reassess as information is received.
If no: does observed information suggest distress or a need for clinical assessment, or need further assessment?
Document facts and gaps; obtain available clarification.
Refer clinical intake information to Nils Ferreira; BTAM team reviews and reassesses.
County Crisis Team; State School-Safety Center
If no: can it be managed with support and monitoring on the available information?
Document disposition and support or monitoring action.
Monitor; reassess with new information. Consider separate conduct-code review when warranted; no automatic police referral.
State School-Safety Center; Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
Is the information insufficient for a confident choice?
Record missing information and obtain available clarification.
Identify BTAM team for review before relying on a clinical referral decision; move to Tier 3 if urgent trigger is indicated.
County Crisis Team; Cavendish Bureau; State School-Safety Center

Cavendish Bureau governs the police threshold. County Crisis Team governs clinical intake only where the police threshold is not indicated. A conduct-code implication alone does not require police action.
Cavendish Bureau; County Crisis Team; Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code

sheets.name: Source crosswalk
rows: Traceability for substantive operating requirements. Source wording was consolidated into one operating standard.

The gold-standard derivation used substantive source columns Provision key, Source group, Topic, and Draft provision. The “Retired helper - do not use” field was excluded from interpretation and did not control any tier, threshold, or referral outcome.
The two CB-04 rows have the same provision key and identical documentation provision. They were consolidated as one operational requirement and are not counted twice.
The separate Records administration inventory, including its legacy archive-status header, is unrelated to BTAM and is excluded from this crosswalk and standard.
Prevention-focused screening, assessment, management, and referral; not conduct policy.
State School-Safety Center; Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
BTAM purpose; assessment is not a disciplinary finding.
Same standard across College activities and premises, expressly for both campuses.
Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
Capture source, observations, affected setting, timing, support; distinguish facts from speculation; no diagnosis.
BTAM review, management, clarification, and reassessment.
State School-Safety Center; County Crisis Team
Multidisciplinary review, continuing management, incomplete intake.
Campus-police urgent path for immediate/ongoing threat or police-action information.
Clinical intake to Nils Ferreira when clinical need is suggested without police trigger.
Clinical intake criteria and information gap handling.
Document concern, decision, rationale, action, and route once.
Duplicate keyed documentation provision consolidated once.
Routine support/monitoring and separate conduct-code consideration; no automatic police action.
State School-Safety Center; Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
Routine screening distinction and conduct-code restraint.

sheets.name: Implementation note
rows: For consistent first-line screening before the second-campus opening.
Use the Standard and Decision aid at either campus whenever Frida Crowther or Dmitri Kaczmarek receives a concern.
A common intake and tier structure keeps campus location from changing the screening basis.
Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code; State School-Safety Center
Check that the record contains observable information, source, affected person or setting, timing, supporting information, tier, rationale, action, and route.
This permits oversight reconstruction of the decision without a diagnosis or unsupported inference.
Check escalation against the governing boundary: urgent police path for the Cavendish Bureau trigger; clinical intake to Nils Ferreira only where that trigger is not indicated.
The review uses the source with the direct police boundary and retains the County Crisis Team clinical condition.
Assign BTAM team review for Tier 2, Tier 3, and an insufficient-information screen; revisit a disposition when new information is received.
Management and reassessment continue after initial screening.
State School-Safety Center; County Crisis Team
Keep conduct-code review distinct from BTAM screening. A conduct implication can be considered separately but does not itself require police action.
This preserves the conduct-code distinction and proportionate routing.
Tallow Creek Community College Conduct Code
Confirm that the tier shown in the case record matches the Decision aid outcome and that the action, referral/review, and follow-up match that tier.

original.grader_hint: Check tier-by-tier for an action, not merely a general statement elsewhere.

criteria.grader_hint: 验证每个层都解析为负责任的路径。

original.criterion: Each defined tier has an associated referral, review, or monitoring path.

criteria.grader_hint: 判断最低层是否具有操作意义和相称性。

criteria.description: 该标准规定了在决定问题是否属于警察问题而不是临床转介给尼尔斯·费雷拉时，以哪个来源为准。

spec.professional_context: Tallow Creek Community College is preparing its police department and threat assessment team for the opening of a second campus. Sgt. Estelle Zalewski is responsible for turning a fragmented draft into a standard that can be used consistently by campus personnel, clinicians, and police supervisors.
difficulty_sources: The supplied draft combines guidance from four institutions with different scopes and does not resolve their overlaps.
The practitioner must turn narrative provisions into usable screening tiers and referral actions without inventing unsupported requirements.
The source contains duplicate keyed provisions, a stale retired helper column, and an unrelated adjacent table that must not be mistaken for source content.

source_file.semantic_content: Create one spreadsheet containing a partially completed BTAM draft assembled from four clearly attributed source groups: a state school-safety center guide, Cavendish Bureau model policy, county crisis-team intake criteria, and the Tallow Creek Community College conduct code. The substantive material must cover purpose and scope, observable concern intake, screening roles, tier concepts or criteria, police and clinical referral boundaries, documentation, follow-up, and campus applicability. Include enough overlapping and differently scoped prose that the worker must reconcile it into one standard. Use the supplied people and organisations where roles are needed: Estelle Zalewski, Frida Crowther, Dmitri Kaczmarek, Eamon Merriweather, and Nils Ferreira; Bellhaven Partners may appear as the assembling firm.

defects.construction: In the substantive main table, include two or more rows with the same source-defined provision key and materially overlapping content. The key must be visible in the source itself and the duplicate must be recognizable as an overlap, not a typo. The duplicate should concern an operational BTAM requirement that belongs once in the final standard.

Include a clearly labeled retired/helper column adjacent to the substantive fields. Populate it with stale classifications that conflict with at least some current substantive source text. The source must visibly indicate that the field is retired or helper-only, but must not provide a replacement rule beyond the substantive fields.

Place a separate, unrelated table beside the substantive BTAM table on the same worksheet. Give it a different subject, such as internal document administration, and include a header string containing an embedded line break. It must be distinguishable by its title and fields so a careful worker can exclude it.

source_file.exclusions: Do not seed any other standard defect: no formula errors, broken references, missing-value trap, malformed dates, inconsistent numeric units, hidden image-only facts, or additional unrelated tables. Do not resolve the substantive policy conflicts in the source.

authoring_plan.transformation: The solver must lightly edit and reshape the supplied narrative provisions into a new operational spreadsheet standard. The final artifact should consolidate duplicate keyed provisions, ignore the retired helper field, exclude the adjacent unrelated table, preserve material source facts with attribution, and make a defensible explicit choice about the police-versus-clinical boundary. The request asks for the components but does not dictate the tier names, exact layout, or unsupported local procedure.
gold_rules: Every substantive requirement in the final standard must be traceable to one of the four source groups or to the supplied brief.
The duplicate key represents one requirement, so it must not generate two operational requirements.
The retired helper column is stale and cannot control a tier, threshold, or referral outcome.
The adjacent table and its line-break header are unrelated and must not appear as BTAM content.
The final standard must preserve the source distinction between behavioral threat assessment, clinical referral, conduct response, and police action while explicitly reconciling their boundary.
The grader should accept different tier labels and layouts when the observable criteria, actions, referrals, documentation, and source rationale are substantively equivalent.
The final workbook must contain a practical decision aid, source crosswalk, and implementation note, with internal agreement among those elements.
authoring_plan.review_method: Build the source workbook with ordinary text cells and formulas only as needed, then create an independent reference standard from the specified semantic rules. Walk every rubric item against the reference workbook, checking source fidelity, explicit defect treatment, operational completeness, internal consistency, and rendered usability. Confirm that no rubric item depends on an unstated literal value or internet fact.

original_instruction:
You are Sgt. Estelle Zalewski with Tallow Creek Community College Police. Dean Eamon Merriweather needs one usable behavioral threat assessment and management screening and referral standard before the second campus opens in January. Bellhaven Partners assembled the working material in `Tallow_Creek_BTAM_source.xlsx`; it combines excerpts and draft provisions associated with the state school-safety center, Cavendish Bureau, the county crisis team, and the college conduct code, but it was never reconciled into an operating document. Create `Tallow_Creek_BTAM_standard.xlsx` in the top level of the working directory where you started, using exactly that filename.

The workbook is for the two-campus BTAM team and must be usable by Frida Crowther and Dmitri Kaczmarek when they receive a concern, by Nils Ferreira when a clinical response may be appropriate, and by campus police when a matter may require police action. Build one concise screening and referral standard from the supplied material. Number the operating requirements within the workbook so a reviewer can follow them. Include the purpose and scope, the people or roles responsible for initial screening and escalation, the information to capture, a clearly defined tier structure, the trigger or decision basis for each tier, the action and referral that each tier starts, documentation and follow-up expectations, and a short section explaining how the standard applies across both campuses.

The four source voices do not use the same thresholds or vocabulary. Preserve the important source facts and identify their sources, but reconcile overlapping provisions into a coherent standard rather than pasting four separate policies together. Where the materials disagree about when a concern is a police matter rather than a clinical referral to Nils Ferreira, state the governing choice plainly and give a brief rationale grounded in the supplied material. Do not present a diagnosis, promise confidentiality, or create a new legal duty that the sources do not support. If a source provision cannot be reconciled confidently, show the uncertainty and identify who must make the decision rather than silently choosing an unsupported fact.

Make the finished workbook easy to audit: include a source or crosswalk area linking substantive requirements to their originating material, a short implementation note for supervisors, and a compact decision aid that someone can use while screening. Keep the prose operational and avoid academic background. Do not copy the unrelated material in the source workbook into the standard, do not rely on any retired or helper field when interpreting the draft, and do not repeat a duplicated provision as if it were two separate requirements. Keep the source workbook unchanged; do not add invented people, campuses, agencies, contact details, thresholds, forms, or codes. Use only the names and organisations supplied in the brief or the source file. The result should be complete enough for oversight review while remaining practical for a first-line supervisor to run before January.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/Tallow_Creek_BTAM_source.xlsx` — Single supplied source workbook containing the partially completed BTAM draft and the source provisions that must be faithfully extracted, attributed, reconciled, and converted into the requested standard.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `Tallow_Creek_BTAM_standard.xlsx` — A single spreadsheet containing the completed two-campus BTAM screening and referral standard, its operational decision aid, source crosswalk, and implementation note. (Write the file into the top level of the starting working directory using exactly the specified filename.; Keep the supplied source workbook unchanged.; Use only facts supported by the supplied workbook and the names and organisations in the brief.; The standard must be readable in spreadsheet form and suitable for oversight review.; Do not reproduce the unrelated adjacent table or use the retired helper field as authority.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.
